craft_notes: Sthāyin: corpse-worked (trust-bearing funeral). Rows: row 4 (trembles as landing: the corpse MOVES). Close: trembles (kampate as landing: trembling closes). Rejected: 'cremation' flat — kept burning-of-corpse (the verse's own rite-word); splitting net-curb-rub — kept the chain (one breath of method).

lines: Whatever raising-rite was told, all of it on the body: full oblation, corpse-burning;
for the deluded, a trust-bearing funeral, by ritual-knowledge-yoga force;
having net-drawn the mantras in withdrawing order, curbed, rubbed, and the rest —
by breath-moving through heart, throat, forehead: lo, the corpse trembles.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tatra yo mṛtoddhāre vidhiḥ uktaḥ sa sarva eva śarīre kartavyaḥ pūrṇāhutyā śavaśarīradāhaḥ mūḍhānāṃ tu pratītirūḍhaye sapratyayām antyeṣṭiṃ kriyājñānayogabalāt kuryāt tatra śavaśarīre saṃhārakrameṇa mantrān nyasya jālakrameṇa ākṛṣya rodhanavedhanaghaṭṭanādi kuryāt prāṇasaṃcārakrameṇa hṛdi kaṇṭhe lalāṭe ca ity evaṃ śavaśarīraṃ kampate

reads_against.argmap: How is the rite done on the body? → The corpse is worked like a ritual ground: burned, convinced, net-drawn, curbed, breathed into trembling.
c1_essence: Whatever raising-rite was told, all done to the body: full-oblation burning, trust-bearing funeral, net-drawn mantras, breath-moving through heart-throat-forehead — till the corpse trembles.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with karuṇa undertow (quiescence carrying compassion) (śama with karuṇā (quiescence with compassion))
